install.question: Do I need to install anything?
install.answer: No. Vibrix runs in your browser: the live alpha is already open and needs no install. Lyrixa is part of the suite and still in development.

privacy.question: Is my audio uploaded to a server?
privacy.answer: Vibrix processes the audio you open locally in your browser. The upcoming Transcriptor will provide its own processing details before it becomes available.

export.question: Can I export a video yet?
export.answer: The development alpha includes experimental MP4 or WebM export, with limitations on layers and effects. It is still being tested and is not part of a published release yet. We’ll update this page when that version ships. A clean output for OBS capture is also available.

rights.question: What music and artwork can I use?
rights.answer: Use your own music and images, or content you have permission to use. You are responsible for the rights to the content you use and publish.

A local way

Comparison.description: Where audio is processed changes the workflow. Here is how the two approaches differ.
Comparison.caption: Local processing in Vibrix compared with a server-rendered workflow
Comparison.note: A comparison of processing approaches, not specific providers or plans. Vibrix’s offline video export is still being tested; suite pricing is not yet defined.

processing.label: Processing
processing.local: Audio analysis and the scene run in your browser.
processing.cloud: The server performs the rendering job it receives.

audio.label: Audio file
audio.local: Vibrix opens the file on your device. No upload is needed.
audio.cloud: The server needs access to the audio to include it in the render.

cost.label: Resources
cost.local: Your device supplies the computing resources.
cost.cloud: The provider supplies the resources; the cost depends on its service.

control.label: Preview
control.local: Adjust the visualizer while the scene keeps playing.
control.cloud: The preview workflow depends on the editor you choose.
